name: find_data_type_insn
prose: Precondition: dloc is a valid data_loc_info (ms, arch, ip, op set), basic_blocks is a list of annotated basic blocks (possibly empty) whose begin/end disasm lines lie in the symbol's annotation source (a block with a begin or end offset of -1 hits BUG_ON), and var_types, cu_die and type_die are usable by the helpers. Postcondition (find_data_type_insn, annotate-data.c:1290-1340): it initializes a local type_state, then walks each block's instructions in order (skipping lines with offset -1), updating the variable state at each instruction's address; when it reaches the instruction whose address equals dloc->ip it returns the result of check_matching_type for that instruction, which can be any enum type_match_result value (for example PERF_TMR_OK, PERF_TMR_BAIL_OUT, PERF_TMR_NO_POINTER, PERF_TMR_BAD_OFFSET, PERF_TMR_NO_TYPE or PERF_TMR_UNKNOWN), and may set *type_die and dloc->type_offset when it reports a match; before reaching that instruction it updates the type state after each instruction. If that instruction is never reached it returns PERF_TMR_UNKNOWN. In both cases the local type state is released with exit_type_state before returning.
note: reviewer (round15) right: check_matching_type's result is returned as-is and can be UNKNOWN or several other values (annotate-data.c:1323-1327, 1054-1287); old prose listed only OK/BAIL_OUT. Earlier reviewer's 'prose says state is initialized by caller' - the function initializes its own local state, which the prose covered.

name: get_pinned_fd
prose: Precondition: name is a non-NULL string used as the last path component under the pinned BPF filter directory. Postcondition (get_pinned_fd, bpf-filter.c:790-803): it formats the path '<sysfs mountpoint>/fs/bpf/<PERF_BPF_FILTER_PIN_PATH>/<name>' with asprintf; if that fails it returns -1 at once. Otherwise it calls bpf_obj_get on the path, frees the path, and returns bpf_obj_get's result unchanged: a non-negative file descriptor that the caller must close, or a negative value (bpf_obj_get returns -errno, via libbpf_err_errno, so it is not necessarily -1).
note: reviewer (round15) right: bpf_obj_get -> bpf_obj_get_opts returns libbpf_err_errno(fd) = -errno on failure (tools/lib/bpf/bpf.c:630-631, libbpf_internal.h:597-600); rounds 0/2 reviewers claiming -1 were wrong. Path is freed on the bpf_obj_get path, not when asprintf fails.

name: contention_begin
prose: Precondition: ctx points to the tracepoint argument array: ctx[0] is the contended lock address and ctx[1] its flags. Postcondition (contention_begin, lock_contention.bpf.c:525-634; BPF program): it returns 0 on every path. It returns 0 without recording if 'enabled' is clear, if can_record(ctx) is false, or if get_tstamp_elem(ctx[1]) returns NULL. Otherwise it stores the current time, ctx[0] and (u32)ctx[1] in that element. If needs_callstack is set: when lock_owner is set it tries to find the owner task and its pid, a zeroed stack buffer from stack_buf, and a task reference via bpf_task_from_pid (skipping the rest if any of these is missing); if they succeed it fetches the owner's stack, releases the task, and looks up owner_data for the lock: when there is no entry or the entry's pid differs it writes a new owner_data entry (count 1) and does not update owner_stat; when the same owner is recorded it increments the count and, only if the owner stack id changed, calls update_owner_stat and stores the new timestamp and stack id. Whether or not the owner part ran, it then stores bpf_get_stackid(ctx, ...) in pelem->stack_id and increments stack_fail if that is negative. If needs_callstack is clear and aggr_mode is LOCK_AGGR_TASK: with lock_owner it sets pelem->flags to the owner's pid, or -1U if no owner task is found, otherwise it uses the current task; when a task is available it calls update_task_data, and if that fails with lock_owner set it sets pelem->flags to -1U. No locks are held and the task reference taken from bpf_task_from_pid is released before the owner_data lookup.
note: reviewer (round15) right: owner_stat is updated only in the same-owner/changed-stack-id branch (bpf.c:591-604), not whenever owner_data is created or updated (588); the stack id is recorded after skip_owner whenever needs_callstack is set. Earlier reviewer's overstatement point also covered.

name: contention_end
prose: Precondition: ctx[0] is the lock address and ctx[1] the lock function's return code (read as s32). Postcondition (contention_end, lock_contention.bpf.c:637-846; BPF program): it returns 0 on every path. It returns 0 at once if 'enabled' is clear. It looks first in the per-cpu tstamp_cpu map: if an element with a nonzero lock exists and its lock differs from ctx[0] it returns 0 with nothing changed, otherwise it uses that element; if there is no active per-cpu element it looks up the per-pid tstamp entry for the current pid and returns 0 if it is missing or its lock differs from ctx[0], otherwise it uses it and remembers to delete it at the end (local pid is set only in this per-pid case, otherwise it stays 0). It computes the duration; if it is negative it increments time_fail and jumps to the final cleanup. Otherwise, when needs_callstack and lock_owner are set and an owner_data entry exists, it calls update_owner_stat and then either deletes that entry if its count is <= 1, or sets its timestamp, decrements its count, and, if the stack_buf lookup succeeds, zeroes the buffer and then: when ctx[1] is negative (and bpf_task_from_pid and the owner task are available) refreshes the owner stack id if it changed; otherwise sets the entry's pid to the local pid variable and its stack_id to -1. It then builds the lock_stat key from aggr_mode (stack id, pid, lock address or cgroup id; an unknown mode returns 0 without updating lock_stat, running the cleanup, clearing pelem->lock or deleting the entry). It looks up the lock_stat entry: if it exists it calls update_contention_data; if not, and data_map_full is set it increments data_fail; otherwise it inserts a new entry (adding lock type and slab cache bits to its flags in address mode), retrying the lookup on -EEXIST, setting data_map_full on -E2BIG, and incrementing data_fail when the insert failed and no entry was found. The final cleanup calls check_lock_delay when lock_delay is set, clears pelem->lock, and deletes the per-pid tstamp entry if one was used.
note: reviewer (round15) right: in the owner_data branch the pid/stack_id assignment for ret >= 0 happens only after the stack_buf lookup succeeded (bpf.c:702-704, 741-749); earlier reviewer's 'ownership transfer updates pid rather than deleting' is covered (entry is deleted only when count <= 1).

name: symbol__disassemble_capstone
prose: Precondition: filename, sym and args are valid (args->ms, args->options set), with notes->src->source initialized. Postcondition (symbol__disassemble_capstone, capstone.c:224-345): when HAVE_LIBCAPSTONE_SUPPORT is not defined it returns -1. Otherwise it returns -1 if args->options->objdump_path is set, and returns errno (the current errno value, as read at that point) if dso__read_symbol returns NULL, with nothing allocated or added. It then adds a header line '<address> <name>:' to notes->src->source; failure to allocate that line returns -1 after freeing code_buf. If capstone_init fails it returns -1 after freeing code_buf, leaving the header line already added in notes->src->source. After a successful init it disassembles the buffer and appends one disasm_line per instruction; if a disasm_line allocation fails mid-way it removes every line in notes->src->source (including the header), closes the capstone handle, frees the instruction array and code_buf and returns -1. If the decoded instructions do not cover the whole buffer (offset != buf_len) it likewise removes all lines and returns -1 after closing the handle, freeing the instruction array and code_buf. Otherwise it returns 0 with the header and instruction lines appended, after closing the handle, freeing the instruction array and code_buf.
note: slice cut the head. Reviewer (round15) mixed: wrong that it returns -1 rather than errno (capstone.c:253-254 'return errno'); right that a capstone_init failure leaves the header line in place because needs_cs_close is false (276-277, 327-341); old prose claimed partially added lines are removed on every -1 path after reading the code.

name: cs_etm_decoder__do_hard_timestamp
prose: Precondition: etmq is a valid queue, elem is the decoder's generic trace element carrying a timestamp, trace_chan_id identifies a trace channel and indx is the trace index (used only in messages). Postcondition (cs_etm_decoder__do_hard_timestamp, cs-etm-decoder.c:282-359): if cs_etm__etmq_get_packet_queue returns NULL for trace_chan_id it returns OCSD_RESP_FATAL_SYS_ERR and changes nothing in the packet queue. Otherwise it converts elem->timestamp to ns (0 stays 0). If the packet queue already has a nonzero next_cs_timestamp it sets cs_timestamp to that old value, sets next_cs_timestamp to the converted timestamp and returns OCSD_RESP_CONT, leaving instr_count unchanged and without flagging the traceid queue. Otherwise it sets cs_timestamp to 0 if the converted timestamp is 0 (with a warning unless the queue is timeless), to 0 with an error message if instr_count / INSTR_PER_NS exceeds the converted timestamp, or else to the larger of the current cs_timestamp and the converted timestamp minus instr_count / INSTR_PER_NS; then in all three cases it sets next_cs_timestamp to the converted timestamp, resets instr_count to 0, flags the traceid queue for timestamp attention via cs_etm__etmq_set_traceid_queue_timestamp and returns OCSD_RESP_WAIT.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the traceid queue is flagged only on the WAIT path (cs-etm-decoder.c:351-358), not on the CONT early return (309-316); the older reviewer's instr_count point (CONT branch leaves it unchanged) was already reflected in the old prose.

name: cs_etm__process_auxtrace_info_full
prose: Precondition: event is an AUXTRACE_INFO record whose priv area starts with the CoreSight global header followed by per-CPU metadata blocks, and session is the open perf session (its time_conv and itrace_synth_opts are used). Postcondition (cs_etm__process_auxtrace_info_full, cs-etm.c:3484-3720; slice cut the head): it returns -EINVAL, without allocating anything, if the CPU count is <= 0, the private size is <= 0, or the CPU count exceeds what the record can hold; -ENOMEM if the metadata pointer array cannot be allocated. It then parses one metadata block per CPU: an unrecognized magic number gives -EINVAL, a block that cannot be created gives -ENOMEM, and a CPU id of INT_MAX or more gives -EINVAL; a total length that does not match the parsed size gives -EINVAL; a failed etm allocation gives -ENOMEM; all of these free the metadata blocks and array and return. Then it initializes the auxtrace queues and sets up each queue; a failure there frees the etm (and the queues once initialized) and the metadata, and returns the error. After installing the callbacks and setting session->auxtrace, a failure of cs_etm__setup_timeless_decoding returns its error directly with the etm, its queues, the metadata and session->auxtrace left allocated and set. A failure of cs_etm__synth_events, cs_etm__queue_aux_records, perf_session__peek_events, cs_etm__map_trace_ids_metadata (only called when no AUX_HW_ID record was found) or cs_etm__create_decoders frees the queues, clears session->auxtrace, frees the etm and the metadata, and returns that error. On success it sets etm->data_queued from etm->queues.populated and returns 0; session->auxtrace then points at the new etm, which owns the metadata and is released by cs_etm__free.
note: slice cut the head (real name cs_etm__process_auxtrace_info_full; the packet name is not a function in cs-etm.c). No reviewer reasons beyond the mechanical name mismatch. The old prose described only the tail; rewritten from the full function.

name: adjust_signedness
prose: Precondition: none (size may be any int). Postcondition (adjust_signedness, data-convert-bt.c:218-253): the function is pure and touches no memory, locks or references. For size 1, 2 or 4 it picks value_mask 0x7f, 0x7fff or 0x7fffffff (all bits below the sign bit of that size); if every bit of value_int at or above the sign bit position (the sign bit and all higher bits, i.e. value_int & ~value_mask) is zero it returns value_int unchanged; otherwise it returns (value_int & value_mask) | ~value_mask, which keeps the bits below the sign bit and sets the sign bit and every higher bit to 1. For size 8 and for any other size value_int is returned unchanged.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the 'unchanged' test is (value_int & ~value_mask) == 0 (line 248), so a value whose only set bit at or above the sign position is the sign bit itself is sign-extended, contrary to the old prose. Contract left empty because earlier generated contracts were falsified by random testing.

name: __FUNC_ADD_NON_SAMPLE_EVENT_CLASS(comm,
prose: Generated function add_comm_event (from __FUNC_ADD_NON_SAMPLE_EVENT_CLASS(comm, ...), data-convert-bt.c:1237-1263). Precondition: cw points to an initialized struct ctf_writer whose stream_class is set and whose data.u32 and data.string field types exist. Postcondition: it creates the event class 'perf_comm'; if bt_ctf_event_class_create returns NULL it returns -1. It then adds the fields pid (u32), tid (u32) and comm (string); if any addition fails it prints an error and returns -1, without releasing the new event class (leaked). It then calls bt_ctf_stream_class_add_event_class; if that returns a nonzero value, that value is returned and the event class reference is not released (leaked). On success it stores the class in cw->comm_class, releases its creation reference with bt_ctf_event_class_put (the stream class holds its own reference) and returns 0. On every failure path cw->comm_class is left unchanged.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against data-convert-bt.c:1237-1263 and 1260-1263; prose essentially unchanged, name set to the macro invocation per method rule 5

name: __FUNC_PROCESS_NON_SAMPLE(comm,
prose: Generated function process_comm_event (from __FUNC_PROCESS_NON_SAMPLE(comm, ...), data-convert-bt.c:874-908). Precondition: tool points to the perf_tool member of a struct convert, sample is valid, and cw->comm_class is a valid event class. Postcondition: it increments c->non_sample_count and adds _event->header.size to c->events_size, then creates a CTF event from cw->comm_class; if creation fails it prints an error and returns -1 (the two counters have already been updated). It sets the clock to sample->time and sets the fields u32 pid, u32 tid and string comm from _event->comm through value_set_* helpers; if any setter returns nonzero it returns -1 without releasing the event (leaked) and without appending it. Otherwise, if ctf_stream(cw, 0) returns a stream, it flushes the stream first when its count is at least STREAM_FLUSH_COUNT, increments the count and appends the event; it then releases the event reference and returns the result of perf_event__process_comm(tool, _event, sample, machine).
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read data-convert-bt.c:867-908 and the invocation near line 910; name set to the macro invocation per method rule 5 (function name is generated)

name: nibbles_to_string
prose: Precondition: buf points to len input bytes, and if out is non-NULL then out_len points to a size_t and out points to at least *out_len writable bytes. Postcondition: returns NtsOk exactly when len is even, every nibble pair is valid hex, the decoded bytes form valid UTF-8, and either out is NULL or the output capacity suffices; on NtsOk with out non-NULL it writes the opening quote, the escaped decoded characters, and the closing quote, and sets *out_len to the number of bytes written, while with out NULL it writes nothing and leaves *out_len unchanged. It returns NtsInvalid for an odd len, an invalid hex nibble, or invalid/incomplete UTF-8, and returns NtsOverflow when out is non-NULL and the initial capacity is zero or the remaining capacity is insufficient for an escaped character or the closing quote; on NtsInvalid or NtsOverflow with out non-NULL, out and *out_len may have been partially modified, and with out NULL no output is written.
note: slice cut the head; real function is nibbles_to_string (demangle-rust-v0.c:542-611); prose re-checked against the code and kept, with the name corrected

name: dso__symtab_origin
prose: Precondition: dso may be NULL. Postcondition (dso__symtab_origin, dso.c:49-76): returns '!' if dso is NULL or dso__symtab_type(dso) is DSO_BINARY_TYPE__NOT_FOUND. Otherwise it returns origin[dso__symtab_type(dso)] from a static table whose highest initialized index is DSO_BINARY_TYPE__OPENEMBEDDED_DEBUGINFO (enum value 20, so the table has 21 entries). For the 19 types listed in the table the result is: KALLSYMS 'k', VMLINUX 'v', JAVA_JIT 'j', DEBUGLINK 'l', BUILD_ID_CACHE 'B', BUILD_ID_CACHE_DEBUGINFO 'D', FEDORA_DEBUGINFO 'f', UBUNTU_DEBUGINFO 'u', MIXEDUP_UBUNTU_DEBUGINFO 'x', OPENEMBEDDED_DEBUGINFO 'o', BUILDID_DEBUGINFO 'b', SYSTEM_PATH_DSO 'd', SYSTEM_PATH_KMODULE 'K', SYSTEM_PATH_KMODULE_COMP 'm', GUEST_KALLSYMS 'g', GUEST_KMODULE 'G', GUEST_KMODULE_COMP 'M', GUEST_VMLINUX 'V', GNU_DEBUGDATA 'n'. The types DSO_BINARY_TYPE__KCORE and DSO_BINARY_TYPE__GUEST_KCORE (enum values 18 and 19) lie inside the table but have no initializer, so the result is the NUL character '�'. The types DSO_BINARY_TYPE__BPF_PROG_INFO, __BPF_IMAGE and __OOL (enum values 21 to 23) are beyond the end of the table, so for them the function reads outside the array (undefined behavior). No locks, references or memory are acquired or released.
note: reviewer (round15) mixed: right that BPF_PROG_INFO/BPF_IMAGE/OOL are beyond the 21-entry table (OPENEMBEDDED_DEBUGINFO, value 20, is the highest initializer; dso.h:64-141), so the read is out of bounds; wrong to include KCORE/GUEST_KCORE there: they are values 18/19, inside the table, giving NUL. Enum values counted from dso.h declaration order.

name: evsel__apply_config_terms
prose: Precondition: evsel has an initialized config_terms list and core.attr, opts is a valid record_opts, and track says whether mmap data tracking applies. Postcondition (evsel__apply_config_terms, evsel.c:1161-1301; returns void): it walks the config terms once. For PERIOD and FREQ terms it sets sample_period (freq 0) or sample_freq (freq 1) and the PERIOD sample bit, except that a weak term is skipped when the user already set an interval (period) or frequency (freq) in opts; TIME sets or clears the TIME sample bit; BRANCH sets BRANCH_STACK and parses the branch string when it is set and not 'no', otherwise clears the bit; MAX_EVENTS sets evsel->max_events; INHERIT sets attr->inherit; OVERWRITE sets attr->write_backward; AUX_OUTPUT sets attr->aux_output. CALLGRAPH, STACK_USER, MAX_STACK and RATIO_TO_PREV terms are only remembered; DRV_CFG, PERCORE, AUX_ACTION, AUX_SAMPLE_SIZE and CFG_CHG terms (and any unknown type) are ignored here. Afterwards, if a callgraph string, a nonzero stack dump size or a nonzero max stack was given, it builds a per-event callchain parameter ('fp' is assumed when only max-stack is given); a callgraph string of 'no' disables it, any other string is parsed with parse_callchain_record and, if that parse fails, it prints an error and returns immediately, so the remaining steps, including the ratio-to-prev step, are not performed. Otherwise it rounds the dump size up to a multiple of 8, resets the evsel's callgraph settings if the global callchain parameter is enabled, and, if the per-event callchain is enabled, sets the ADDR and DATA_SRC sample bits and attr.mmap_data = track for DWARF mode and calls evsel__config_callchain. Finally, if a ratio-to-prev term was present, it calls evsel__apply_ratio_to_prev.
note: reviewer (round15) right: 'every config term is applied' was false: DRV_CFG, PERCORE, AUX_ACTION, AUX_SAMPLE_SIZE, CFG_CHG have empty cases (evsel.c:1230-1244); earlier reviewer's early-return point (1270-1275) was already in the old prose and is kept. Also added the BRANCH term and the weak-term skip.

name: evsel__parse_sample
prose: Precondition: evsel, event and data are valid pointers; event points to a complete record whose header.size is the real record length. Postcondition (evsel__parse_sample, evsel.c:3067-3425; slice cut the head, the packet name perf_evsel__parse_sample does not exist): it first clears *data and sets defaults (cpu/pid/tid -1, ids and time -1, period from the attr, cpumode and misc from the header, data_src none, vcpu -1). For a record that is not PERF_RECORD_SAMPLE it returns 0 when the evsel has no sample_id_all, otherwise the result of perf_evsel__parse_id_sample (0). For a PERF_RECORD_SAMPLE it returns -EFAULT if perf_event__check_size fails against the evsel's sample_size, and then fills the fields selected by sample_type in order, returning -EFAULT when an OVERFLOW_CHECK shows a field running past the record end (read format values, callchain, raw data, branch stack, branch counters, user and interrupt registers, user stack, weight, data source, transaction, aux data), when the read-group, callchain or branch-stack count is too large, or when the user stack dump size reported exceeds the requested size; on such a failure data may be partially filled. When the evsel needs byte swapping, it byte-swaps the tid and cpu words it reads into data and swaps the raw data, branch flags and aux data inside the event buffer in place. Pointers stored in data (read group values, callchain, raw data, branch stack, registers, user stack data, aux data) point into the event buffer. For an off-cpu event it finally returns __set_offcpu_sample's result (0, or -EFAULT when raw data is missing or too short), which overwrites pid, tid, period, callchain, ip and cgroup from the raw data; otherwise it returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; real name evsel__parse_sample. No reviewer claim beyond the mechanical name check. Old prose omitted non-sample records, the in-place byte swap and the off-cpu path, and described max_size as a parameter (it is event->header.size).

name: parse_hwmon_filename
prose: Precondition: filename is a NUL-terminated string, type and number are writable pointers, item may be NULL, and when item is non-NULL alarm is a writable pointer. Postcondition (parse_hwmon_filename, hwmon_pmu.c:157-219): it copies at most the first 23 characters of filename into a local buffer and scans that copy for the first digit or '_'. At a digit it ends the type text there, stores strtoul of the digit run (converted to int) in *number and points the item text after the digits, skipping one '_' if present; at a '_' it ends the type text there, stores -1 in *number and points the item text after the '_'. It returns false if no digit or '_' was found in those 23 characters (nothing written), if the type text is empty, or if item is non-NULL and the item text is empty. It then looks the type text up in the hwmon type table (excluding index 0) and returns false if it is not there (*number may already have been written, *type is not). If found it writes the table index to *type; with item == NULL it returns true at this point without touching *item or *alarm. Otherwise it sets *alarm to false; if the item text is longer than 6 characters and ends in '_alarm' it replaces the item text by a copy with that suffix removed (truncated to 23 characters) and sets *alarm to true; it looks the item text up in the hwmon item table (excluding index 0): if not found it returns false (after *type was written and with *alarm possibly already true), otherwise it writes the item index to *item and returns true.
note: reviewer (round15) right: when the item lookup fails the function returns false after *type was already written (hwmon_pmu.c:197, 210-216), contrary to the old 'without writing *type'; round-1 and round-2 reviewer points (item==NULL returns true after the type matches; *alarm stays true on item failure) were already in the old prose and kept.

name: evsel__hwmon_pmu_open
prose: Precondition: evsel belongs to a hwmon PMU whose config encodes the hwmon type and number, threads is the thread map, and evsel->core.fd has entries for cpu map indices start_cpu_map_idx to end_cpu_map_idx-1 and every thread. Postcondition (slice cut the head; evsel__hwmon_pmu_open, hwmon_pmu.c:762-809): it opens the PMU's hwmon directory; if that fails it returns -errno and nothing else is touched. Otherwise, for each cpu index in [start_cpu_map_idx, end_cpu_map_idx) and each thread, it opens '<type><num>_input' relative to the directory and stores the resulting descriptor in the evsel's fd array. If all opens succeed it closes the directory and returns 0. If an open fails it sets err to -errno, records the failing thread index in threads->err_thread, and then closes every non-negative descriptor stored for the earlier threads of the current cpu index and for all threads of every lower cpu index down to index 0 (not only down to start_cpu_map_idx), setting each of those entries to -1; the failing slot keeps the negative descriptor and later slots are untouched. It then closes the directory and returns the negative errno.
note: slice cut the head; real function evsel__hwmon_pmu_open (the item was an unnamed loop excerpt). Note the cleanup loop 'while (--idx >= 0)' (hwmon_pmu.c:806) goes below start_cpu_map_idx; the old prose said only 'all previously opened fds' and omitted the directory-open failure. Not a reviewer claim.

name: intel_pt_walk_insn
prose: Precondition: decoder is a valid decoder with walk_insn set, intel_pt_insn is a writable instruction record and ip is the stop address (0 for none). Postcondition (intel_pt_walk_insn, intel-pt-decoder.c:1158-1265): it sets mtc_insn, computes max_insn_cnt via intel_pt_next_sample and calls decoder->walk_insn, then adds the walked instruction count to tot_insn_cnt, timestamp_insn_cnt, sample_insn_cnt and period_insn_cnt. If walk_insn fails it resets no_progress, sets pkt_state to INTEL_PT_STATE_ERR2 and returns -ENOLINK if the error was -ENOENT, otherwise -EILSEQ, without recording instruction state in decoder->state. Otherwise, if ip is nonzero and decoder->ip equals ip the result is -EAGAIN; else, if a sample period was due (max_insn_cnt nonzero and the count reached it) it calls intel_pt_sample_insn, and then by instruction kind: a non-branch instruction sets state type INTEL_PT_INSTRUCTION with from_ip = ip and to_ip = 0, advances decoder->ip by the length and the result is INTEL_PT_RETURN (1); a call (other than a zero-length unconditional one) pushes the return address and, if intel_pt_push fails, that error is the result; a return pops decoder->ret_addr; an unconditional branch sets from_ip/to_ip, advances ip by length plus relative offset, makes the result INTEL_PT_RETURN, and runs the stuck-loop check, which on a never-ending loop sets pkt_state to INTEL_PT_STATE_ERR_RESYNC and makes the result -ELOOP; any other branch (conditional or indirect) leaves the result 0. For all these results the function then (except for the unconditional-branch path that does not reset it) clears no_progress, records the instruction op, length and bytes in decoder->state, sets INTEL_PT_IN_TX in state.flags when a transaction is active, and returns the result.
note: reviewer (round15) right: indirect branches also return 0 (conditional and indirect branches both fall to 'out' with err 0, intel-pt-decoder.c:1217-1253) and intel_pt_sample_insn is called when the sample period is reached (1192-1193); earlier reviewer's 0-for-conditional and push-error points were already in the old prose.

name: intel_pt_fup_event
prose: Precondition: decoder is a valid decoder; its pending FUP flags (set_fup_cfe_ip, set_fup_cfe, set_fup_mode_exec, set_fup_tx_flags, set_fup_ptw, set_fup_mwait, set_fup_pwre, set_fup_exstop, set_fup_bep) and overflow may be set; no_tip says whether the FUP was not followed by a TIP. Postcondition (intel_pt_fup_event, intel-pt-decoder.c:1315-1410): it saves state.type, clears INTEL_PT_BRANCH from state.type and sets state.insn_op to OTHER and insn_len to 0 (these two stay changed even when it returns false). For each pending flag it clears the flag and adds the corresponding event to decoder->state: CFE (type EVT, plus BRANCH again when no ip was given and pge is set, with cfe type, vector, evd and the FUP_IP flag when ip or pge), mode-exec (calls intel_pt_sample_iflag and remembers to sample the FUP instruction when no_tip), transaction flags (TRANSACTION, plus BRANCH again for an abort, and state.flags is set to the TX flags), PTW, MWAIT, PWRE, EXSTOP and BEP; each one makes the result true. If overflow was pending it is cleared; if no event was consumed and pge was false it sets pge, sets state.type to include BRANCH | TRACE_BEGIN (first zeroing the type and setting pkt_state to INTEL_PT_STATE_RESAMPLE when hop is set), sets from_ip to 0 and to_ip to decoder->ip, and returns true at once. Otherwise, if at least one event was consumed, it sets from_ip to decoder->ip and to_ip to 0, calls intel_pt_sample_fup_insn when that was requested, and returns true; if none was consumed it restores state.type to the saved value and returns false.
note: reviewer (round15) right: INTEL_PT_BRANCH is added back for CFE without ip, for transaction aborts and for the overflow trace-begin (intel-pt-decoder.c:1331-1332, 1352-1353, 1395); old prose said it was cleared. The older reviewer's overflow/from_ip/to_ip point was already in the old prose; insn_op/insn_len staying modified on false added.

name: intel_pt_walk_fup
prose: Precondition: decoder is a valid decoder positioned at a FUP packet with last_ip set. Postcondition (intel_pt_walk_fup, intel-pt-decoder.c:1421-1462): it repeatedly calls intel_pt_walk_insn starting from decoder->last_ip as the stop address. If the call returns INTEL_PT_RETURN (1, which walk_insn uses for a walked non-branch or unconditional-branch instruction) it returns 0. If it returns -EAGAIN (the stop address was reached), or intel_pt_fup_with_nlip holds (FUP_WITH_NLIP flag, no error, an indirect branch whose end address equals the stop address), it records no_tip = (pkt_state != INTEL_PT_STATE_FUP), sets pkt_state to INTEL_PT_STATE_IN_SYNC, calls intel_pt_fup_event(decoder, no_tip) and returns 0 if that returned true and no_tip is true, otherwise -EAGAIN. For any other result it first clears set_fup_tx_flags; a nonzero error is then returned as is; an indirect branch or a conditional branch sets pkt_state to INTEL_PT_STATE_ERR_RESYNC and returns -ENOENT; any other instruction calls intel_pt_bug() and the loop continues.
note: reviewer (round15) right: set_fup_tx_flags is cleared (line 1442) before the error return at 1443-1444, not only on 'successful' steps; round-1 reviewer's point (returns 0 also when fup_event consumed an event and no_tip) was already in the old prose; old prose misdescribed INTEL_PT_RETURN as 'a return'.

name: intel_pt_fast_forward
prose: Precondition: decoder is a valid decoder with its lookahead callback set; timestamp is the target time. Postcondition (intel_pt_fast_forward, intel-pt-decoder.c:4451-4515): it calls decoder->lookahead with intel_pt_ff_cb to find the buffer timestamp of the buffer to fast forward to; a negative result is returned at once. If a buffer timestamp was found it repeatedly advances decoder->pos by the current length and calls intel_pt_get_next_data until decoder->buf_timestamp equals it; any nonzero result other than -ENOLINK is returned immediately, while -ENOLINK (non-consecutive trace) is ignored; this walk moves the decoder's position and buffer even if no PSB is found afterwards. If the decoder then has no buffer, or no PSB is found in it, it returns 0. Otherwise it walks successive PSBs: while a PSB's TSC (extended with the buffer timestamp) is less than timestamp, it moves decoder->pos, buf and len to that PSB and calls intel_pt_reposition; it stops at the first PSB with no TSC or a TSC not below timestamp, or when there are no more PSBs, and returns 0.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the buffer-timestamp walk (intel-pt-decoder.c:4466-4475) advances decoder->pos/buf before the PSB search, so the decoder is not 'unchanged' when no PSB or TSC is found; the older reviewer's -ENOLINK tolerance point was already in the old prose.

name: intel_pt_setup_queue
prose: Precondition: pt and queue are valid and queue_nr is the queue's index. Postcondition (intel_pt_setup_queue, intel-pt.c:1575-1655): it returns 0 immediately if the queue has no buffers (nothing allocated). If queue->priv is NULL it allocates an intel_pt_queue (returning -ENOMEM on failure), stores it in queue->priv and initializes its cpu, tid, cbr_seen, step_through_buffers, sync_switch and time range; this happens before the checks below, so it can also occur on the timeless path. Then, only if the queue is not already on the heap and it is not (sync_switch with switch_state EXPECTING_SWITCH_EVENT): if pt->timeless_decoding is set it returns 0 (the allocated ptq is kept); otherwise, if sel_start and sel_timestamp are set it calls intel_pt_fast_forward and returns a nonzero result; then it calls intel_pt_decode repeatedly, skipping states with an error other than INTEL_PT_ERR_NODATA, until a state with a timestamp is found; on INTEL_PT_ERR_NODATA it returns 0 without adding the queue to the heap. With a timestamp it stores it and the state in the ptq, sets have_sample (cleared if the timestamp is before sel_timestamp when a selection start is set), calls intel_pt_sample_flags and adds the queue to the heap with auxtrace_heap__add: a nonzero result is returned (on_heap stays false), otherwise on_heap is set. In all other cases (already on the heap, or expecting a switch event) it returns 0.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the ptq allocation (-ENOMEM) happens before the timeless_decoding check (intel-pt.c:1584-1588 vs 1611-1612). Round-0 reviewer's empty-queue/already-on-heap points are covered; old prose also missed that non-NODATA decode errors are skipped in the loop.

name: symbol__disassemble_bpf_libbfd
prose: Precondition: sym and args are valid, args->ms->map's dso describes a BPF program, and the symbol's annotation source list (notes->src->source) is initialized. Postcondition (symbol__disassemble_bpf_libbfd, libbfd.c:496-660; slice cut the head and the name symbol__disassemble_bpf does not appear in the file): when HAVE_LIBBPF_SUPPORT is not defined it returns SYMBOL_ANNOTATE_ERRNO__NO_LIBOPCODES_FOR_BPF. Otherwise it returns SYMBOL_ANNOTATE_ERRNO__BPF_INVALID_FILE at once if the dso's binary type is not DSO_BINARY_TYPE__BPF_PROG_INFO. It then opens perf's own executable with libbfd (abort() if bfd_openr fails or the file is not a bfd object), and opens a memstream; if that fails it sets ret to errno and goes to out. It finds the BPF prog info node and returns (via out) SYMBOL_ANNOTATE_ERRNO__BPF_MISSING_BTF if there is none, or if the jited instructions array or, later, the jited ksyms array was not converted (flag bits missing in info_linear->arrays); it aborts if no disassembler can be obtained. Otherwise it disassembles the jited code instruction by instruction until a disassembler step returns count <= 0 or pc reaches the symbol length: for each instruction, when hide_src_code is off and a BTF source line was found for the address, it appends a source line, then appends the disassembled line (failures to allocate a disasm_line just skip that line). It then sets ret to 0. At out it frees the prog_linfo and btf, closes the memstream and frees its buffer if the memstream was opened, closes the bfd, and returns ret.
note: slice cut the head; real function symbol__disassemble_bpf_libbfd. Packet prose re-read against libbfd.c:496-660; old statement kept in substance, with the no-libbpf return corrected (the #ifdef is HAVE_LIBBPF_SUPPORT) and failure handling of disasm_line__new added. No reviewer claim except the mechanical name mismatch.

name: machine__is_lock_function
prose: Precondition: machine points to an initialized machine whose kernel maps can be searched by symbol name; addr is an address. Postcondition (machine__is_lock_function, machine.c:3260-3322; slice cut the head): on the first call (machine->sched.text_start == 0) it looks up the kernel symbol __sched_text_start; if that symbol is not found it stores the sentinel 1 in machine->sched.text_start and returns false. Otherwise it fills in machine->sched.text_start/text_end from __sched_text_start/__sched_text_end and machine->lock.text_start/text_end from __lock_text_start/__lock_text_end (these three later lookups are dereferenced without a NULL check), and fills machine->traceiter and machine->trace ranges from __traceiter_contention_begin and trace_contention_begin when those symbols exist. In every call, after that: it returns false if machine->sched.text_start equals the sentinel 1; otherwise it returns true if addr lies in [sched.text_start, sched.text_end), or in [lock.text_start, lock.text_end), or (when traceiter.text_start is nonzero) in [traceiter.text_start, traceiter.text_end), or (when trace.text_start is nonzero) in [trace.text_start, trace.text_end); in every other case it returns false. The function modifies machine on the first call (and does not change it afterwards); it acquires no locks or references.
note: slice cut the head; the real function is machine__is_lock_function (machine.c:3260). The old prose (an unnamed predicate) omitted the first-call initialization of the sched/lock/traceiter/trace ranges and the sentinel; a drop is not warranted because the function exists.

name: parse_perf_probe_point
prose: Precondition: arg is NULL or a writable NUL-terminated probe specification that the function modifies in place (delimiters are overwritten with NULs), and pev points to a perf_probe_event whose point fields are expected to be zero/NULL on entry. Postcondition (parse_perf_probe_point, probe-event.c:1495-1707): it returns -EINVAL if arg is NULL. For an SDT event (is_sdt_event) it sets pev->sdt, and if the spec contains a delimiter other than '@' it returns -EINVAL; with '@' it sets pev->target (a newly allocated string, -ENOMEM on failure) and then returns the result of parse_perf_probe_event_name, and on success sets point.function to '%<event>' with asprintf (a failure there returns -errno); the SDT branch returns without parsing or checking any other point field. For other specs: an 'EVENT=' prefix is parsed with parse_perf_probe_event_name (a negative result is returned); the next part is stored as pp->file if it looks like a file spec (no '+@%', a ':' or ';' after a '.') or as pp->function otherwise (allocation failure gives -ENOMEM, and nothing is stored if that part is empty); a function that starts with '0x' is also parsed as pp->abs_address and -EINVAL is returned if trailing characters remain. The remaining parts are then parsed: ';' stores the rest as lazy_line (-ENOMEM on failure), ':' a line number and '+' an offset (-EINVAL on non-numeric text), '@' a file (-EINVAL if one is already set, '*' is ignored, -ENOMEM on failure), '%return' sets retprobe and any other '%' place returns -ENOTSUP. Finally it returns -EINVAL if lazy_line is combined with line or offset, if line is combined with offset, if only a file is given with no line or lazy pattern and no function, if offset is given without a function, or if offset, line or lazy pattern is combined with a return probe; otherwise it returns 0. On success pev->event, pev->target, point.function, point.file and point.lazy_line are set only when the specification supplied them (they may stay NULL); strings that were allocated stay owned by pev, and on any failure pev and pev->point may be left partially filled.
note: reviewer (round15) right: pev->event and the point strings are set only when present in the specification (e.g. function stays NULL for an empty function part, event is set only by an EVENT= prefix or the SDT path); old prose also implied the consistency checks apply to SDT specs, but the SDT branch returns earlier (probe-event.c:1519-1542).

name: s390_cpumsf_run_decoder
prose: Precondition: sfq is a valid decoder queue whose queue_nr indexes a valid auxtrace queue, and *ts holds the cutoff timestamp up to which entries may be processed. Postcondition (s390_cpumsf_run_decoder, s390-cpumsf.c:695-767): if sfq->buffer is NULL it takes the next buffer of the queue; if there is none it sets *ts to ~0ULL and returns 1 (queue done). A new buffer gets use_size/use_data initialized and its data is logged if a log file is open. If the buffer has no data it is read; failure returns -ENOMEM with sfq->buffer still pointing at the buffer and *ts unchanged. It then calls s390_cpumsf_samples(sfq, ts). If that returns 0 (the buffer is only partly consumed, or its first trailer timestamp is later than *ts) the buffer stays in sfq->buffer and the function returns 0. If it returns a nonzero value the buffer is unlinked from the queue list, freed and sfq->buffer is set to NULL; a positive value (buffer fully scanned, including the case of an invalid trailer time) is converted to 0, and a negative value (-1 when the buffer fails validation, -EBADF when an entry cannot be turned into an event) is returned. *ts is updated by s390_cpumsf_samples: to ~0ULL when the buffer fails validation or its trailer time is invalid, to the timestamp of the page trailer reached (the one that exceeded *ts, or the last one read before an -EBADF) in the other cases, and it is left unchanged only on the -ENOMEM return.
note: reviewer (round15) right: on -EBADF from s390_cpumsf_samples, *ts is the last aux_ts (s390-cpumsf.c:642-643, 668-669), not ~0ULL; the old prose also said '~0ULL on error' for all errors and omitted the 0 return with a partly consumed buffer. Round-0 reviewer's points (negative sample-processing returns; -ENOMEM leaves sfq->buffer set) were already in the old prose.

name: print_l1d_miss
prose: Precondition: config, evsel and out point to valid objects, aggr_idx is a valid aggregation index and misses is the L1 data-cache miss count for that aggregation. Postcondition (print_l1d_miss, stat-shadow.c:246-255; the packet name print_l1_miss does not exist and the slice cut the head; returns void): it calls print_ratio(config, evsel, aggr_idx, misses, out, STAT_L1_DCACHE, {20.0, 10.0, 5.0}, "of all L1-dcache accesses"). print_ratio looks up the STAT_L1_DCACHE denominator with find_stat; if both misses and that denominator are nonzero it computes the ratio 100.0 * misses / denominator, classifies it against the thresholds, and passes it with the format "%7.2f%%" and the unit text; otherwise it passes a ratio of 0, an unknown threshold class and NULL format and unit. In both cases it calls out->print_metric exactly once. print_l1d_miss has no other side effects.
note: real function is print_l1d_miss (print_l1_miss does not exist in stat-shadow.c); the old prose's 'or emits nothing' is replaced by print_ratio's exact behavior (stat-shadow.c:192-211); not a reviewer claim.

name: svg_build_topology_map
prose: Precondition: env->nr_sibling_cores and env->nr_sibling_threads give the number of NUL-terminated strings packed back to back in env->sibling_cores and env->sibling_threads, and env->nr_cpus_online is the number of online CPUs. Postcondition (svg_build_topology_map, svghelper.c:752-811; slice cut the head, the name in the packet is not a function in the file): it sets nr_cpus to min(env->nr_cpus_online, MAX_NR_CPUS) and returns 0 on success or -1 (ret starts as -1 and is set to 0 only at the end). It allocates two arrays of cpumask_t with calloc, one entry per sibling core string and per sibling thread string; if either allocation fails it prints a message and returns -1. It converts each sibling string to a bitmap with str_to_bitmap (limited to nr_cpus); a failure prints a message and returns -1. It then mallocs the global topology_map with nr_cpus ints; if that fails it prints a message and returns -1 with topology_map left as NULL and topology_map_size unchanged. On success it sets topology_map_size to nr_cpus, sets every entry to -1 and fills the map with scan_core_topology. On every path the two temporary arrays are freed before returning. On the calloc and parse failures topology_map is not touched.
note: slice cut the head; real function svg_build_topology_map. Old prose said 'ret holds the caller's initial failure value': ret is a local initialized to -1 (svghelper.c:757) and the function takes env as its only parameter.

name: dso__load_sym_internal
prose: Precondition: dso, map, syms_ss and runtime_ss are valid; syms_ss has the symbol table selected by dynsym (symtab when dynsym is 0, dynsym otherwise), kmodule says whether this is a kernel module, and for a kernel dso map has a kmap whose maps are available. Postcondition (dso__load_sym_internal, symbol-elf.c:1506-1786; the slice shows this internal loader, not its wrapper dso__load_sym at 1788): it returns the number of symbols it inserted into the dso's symbol tree(s) (>= 0), or -1. It returns -1 at once if the dso is a kernel dso whose kmap has no maps, and returns -1 (after releasing the current dso reference) when elf_getdata/elf_getscn fails for the symbol table, its string table or either section-name string table, when elf_getscn fails for a symbol's section (in the symbol file or, for NOBITS sections, in the runtime file), when dso__process_kernel_symbol returns nonzero, or when symbol__new fails; in those cases symbols already inserted stay inserted. Before the loop it updates dso text offset/end from the runtime '.text' section, may set the kernel reference-relocation values and the map relocation (also for the vdso), and sets the dso's adjust_symbols flag. In the loop it skips symbols that fail the symbol/label filters, ARM and RISC-V mapping symbols, absolute symbols, symbols in sections without SHF_ALLOC and labels failing the section filter; it adjusts addresses for OPD, thumb functions, kernel symbols (via dso__process_kernel_symbol) or via program headers when adjusting symbols, demangles the name, creates the symbol and inserts it into the (possibly module-specific) dso's tree, incrementing the count. If at least one symbol was inserted it then fixes up symbol end addresses and duplicates, and the kernel maps' ends for a kernel dso, and returns the count.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the annotation described the wrapper dso__load_sym (symbol-elf.c:1788-1843, which calls this function up to three times), but the slice shows the internal loader; item is fixed as dso__load_sym_internal, and the wrapper (returns -1 for a kernel dso without symtab or a failing internal call, else the summed count) is not described by this prose.

name: thread_stack__x86_retpoline
prose: Precondition: ts->crp is valid and the stack holds at least three entries (the only caller checks ts->cnt > 2); to_al is the branch target location and sample the current sample. Postcondition (thread_stack__x86_retpoline, thread-stack.c:1049-1099): let sym be the symbol of the top entry's call path and tsym the target symbol. If sym is an x86 retpoline function the top entry is popped (ts->cnt is decremented); then, if the symbol of the entry now below the new top exists, equals tsym and the target address is not tsym's start, that entry is popped as well and the function returns 0 without creating a call path. Otherwise (sym not a retpoline), if sym is non-NULL and equals tsym, the top entry is popped and the function returns 0 without creating a call path. In the remaining cases (the retpoline whose pop did not trigger the second pop, or a top symbol different from tsym) it creates a call path for tsym with call_path__findnew, with the entry below the top as parent, and returns -ENOMEM if that fails; otherwise it stores that call path in the top-of-stack entry and returns 0.
note: reviewer (round15) right: when the top symbol equals the target symbol (and is not a retpoline) the entry is popped and 0 is returned, not replaced (thread-stack.c:1081-1087); the older reviewer's 3-entry and pop-then-return-0 points were already in the old prose.

name: thread_stack__process
prose: Precondition: thread, comm, sample, from_al, to_al and crp are valid; sample->cpu selects the thread stack; sample->flags may contain any of the CALL, RETURN, TRACE_BEGIN, TRACE_END and BRANCH bits (a CALL may also carry TRACE_END). Postcondition (thread_stack__process, thread-stack.c:1101-1230): it finds the stack for sample->cpu; a stack without a call-return processor is reset and replaced, and a missing stack is created (-ENOMEM if allocation fails). When the comm differs and the thread is the main thread (pid == tid) it flushes the stack and returns any error from the flush. If the stack is empty it calls thread_stack__bottom and returns its error. After these steps it always increments branch_count, adds the sample's insn_cnt and cyc_cnt and sets last_time (so these are updated even when the sample then changes nothing on the stack). It then dispatches on the flags: CALL returns 0 with no push if ip or addr is zero or the call is zero-length, else pushes a call path (a push error is returned; a successful push may mark a possible x86 retpoline); RETURN returns 0 with no change if addr is zero and the sample is not a syscall/interrupt return, pops the kernel stack for such a return, returns 0 with no change if ip is zero, calls thread_stack__x86_retpoline when a retpoline was detected, the stack has more than 2 entries and the top return address differs from the target, and otherwise pops via thread_stack__pop_cp (a negative result is returned; a positive result is handled by thread_stack__no_call_return); TRACE_BEGIN and TRACE_END call their helpers; a BRANCH to the start of a different symbol pushes a jump entry marked non_call. The function returns the 0, or the error or result of the helper called on that path.
note: reviewer (round15) right: several paths return 0 early without changing the stack (zero ip/addr or zero-length calls, returns with no addr/ip), thread-stack.c:1154-1159, 1177-1189; older reviewer's CALL+TRACE_END point was already in the old prose. Counters/last_time are updated before the dispatch.

name: main
prose: Precondition: argc/argv hold the command line; the global option variables are filled in by parse_options (which may itself exit the process on bad options). Postcondition (main, pfrut.c:198-438): it returns 1 with nothing opened if getuid() is not 0; it opens /dev/acpi_pfr_update0 (return 1 on failure) and /dev/acpi_pfr_telemetry0 (return 1 on failure, without closing the already open update descriptor). With query_cap it queries the update capabilities (printing them on success), closes both descriptors and returns the ioctl result (0, or the failing ioctl's -1). With log_getinfo it reads the telemetry data info and info, prints them, and returns 0, or returns 1 after closing both descriptors if either ioctl fails (on success it returns without closing the descriptors). Otherwise it builds a log-info request (an invalid level, type or revid only prints a message and leaves that field at -1), and returns 1 after closing both descriptors if PFRT_LOG_IOC_SET_INFO fails, if set_revid is given and PFRU_IOC_SET_REV fails, or if a capsule file is named and its open, fstat or mmap fails (closing the capsule descriptor where it was opened), or its write returns -1 (the mapping is not unmapped on that path). A successful capsule load unmaps and closes it. For action values 1, 2 and 3 it performs the stage, activate or stage-and-activate ioctl and prints its result without checking it, so an ioctl failure does not change main's return value; any other nonzero action closes both descriptors and returns 1. It then closes the update descriptor; with log_read it returns 1 (after closing the log descriptor) if the data-info ioctl fails, the maximum data size is zero, the buffer malloc fails, or the mmap fails (the buffer is not freed on that last path); otherwise it copies and prints the telemetry log. Finally it closes the log descriptor and returns 0.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the action ioctl result is only printed (pfrut.c:373-386), so main still returns 0 after a failed stage/activate; also corrected: the telemetry open failure returns 1 without closing fd_update (222-226), and not-root returns before anything is opened.

name: string_to_frequency
prose: Precondition: str is a non-NULL NUL-terminated string. Postcondition (string_to_frequency, cpufreq-set.c:62-142): it skips leading '0' characters, then scans digits and '.' characters; a second '.' in that run makes it return 0. If characters remain after that run, they are treated as a unit suffix: the suffix must be a case-insensitive prefix of exactly one of the unit names 'hz', 'khz', 'mhz', 'ghz', 'thz' (so for example 'h', 'k', 'MHz' are accepted, not only the full names), otherwise it returns 0; a missing suffix means kHz. The unit gives the power of ten by which the number is scaled to kHz (hz -3, khz 0, mhz 3, ghz 6, thz 9). It returns 0 if there are no digits to convert, or if the digits after scaling and padding would need 32 or more characters; otherwise it builds the scaled digit string, drops its last digit (using that digit, if it is '5' or greater, to round the value up by one, so halves round up and digits further to the right are ignored) and converts it with strtoul: if strtoul sets errno (overflow, ERANGE) it returns 0; otherwise it returns the converted value plus one when rounding up, except that a value of ULONG_MAX is not incremented. A result that rounds to zero is returned as 0.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the suffix test accepts any case-insensitive prefix of exactly one unit name (cpufreq-set.c:83-94), so 'h', 'k', 'm', 'g', 't' work, not only the full names; rest of the old prose re-checked.

name: cmd_freq_set
prose: Precondition: argc/argv are the 'cpupower frequency-set' command line and the file-scope chosen-CPU mask cpus_chosen is initialized. Postcondition (cmd_freq_set, cpufreq-set.c:196-339; slice cut the head, it shows only the tail of the function): it parses the options with getopt_long and returns -EINVAL (after printing a message) for an unknown option, for a -d, -u or -f value for which string_to_frequency returns 0, and for a governor name shorter than 3 or longer than 18 characters or not readable by sscanf; repeated options are counted in double_parm. After parsing it prints a message and returns -EINVAL if any parameter was repeated, if -f is combined with -d/-u/-g, or if none of -f, -d, -u, -g was given; no CPU is modified in those cases. Otherwise it sets the chosen-CPU mask to all CPUs when it is empty. With -r it walks the chosen CPUs that are online and adds the related CPUs of each to the mask, stopping the walk entirely (mask partially updated) if cpufreq_get_related_cpus returns NULL for some CPU; for each list it obtains it calls cpufreq_put_related_cpus with its pointer at the list's last element, after the loop that follows ->next. It then calls get_cpustate and, for every chosen CPU that is online, prints 'Setting cpu: N' and calls do_one_cpu; for the first CPU where do_one_cpu returns nonzero it prints an error and returns that value (without printing the offline-CPU report). If all succeed it prints the offline CPUs report and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head; real function cmd_freq_set (the item was an unnamed function). The old prose started from the parameter check and covered the tail only; rewritten from the full function. Not a reviewer claim (dropped item).

name: hfi_main
prose: Precondition: none; the function uses the global driver state drv and the global exit flag _hfi_exit. Postcondition (hfi_main, hfi-events.c:244-303; slice cut the head, the packet name hfi_init is not a function in the file): it returns -1 with a message if the CPU does not report HFI support (CPUID leaf 6, EAX bit 19), and returns -1 if nl_socket_alloc fails; in both cases nothing is allocated. If genl_connect fails it frees the socket and returns -1 (drv is not yet modified). Otherwise it stores the socket in drv.nl_handle and a freshly allocated callback set in drv.nl_cb; if nl_cb_alloc, nl_get_multicast_id or nl_socket_add_membership then fails it frees the socket with nl_socket_free and returns -1, leaving drv.nl_handle pointing at the freed socket and drv.nl_cb (when allocated) not released. On success it installs the sequence-check and valid-message handlers and loops on nl_recvmsgs until _hfi_exit becomes nonzero or nl_recvmsgs returns a nonzero value; it then returns 0 without freeing the socket or the callbacks, and a nonzero nl_recvmsgs value is not returned to the caller.
note: slice cut the head; real function hfi_main (hfi_init does not exist in hfi-events.c). Old prose omitted the CPUID HFI check and the stale drv.nl_handle pointer after failures; the leak of the callback is stated in the source comment at line 298. Not a reviewer claim (mechanical name mismatch only).

name: set_cpufreq_scaling_min_max_from_cpuinfo
prose: Precondition: cpu is a CPU number, present_cpumask_size/present_cpumask describe the present CPUs, cpuinfo_max selects cpuinfo_max_freq (nonzero) or cpuinfo_min_freq (zero) as the source file, and scaling_max selects scaling_max_freq (nonzero) or scaling_min_freq (zero) as the file to write. Postcondition (set_cpufreq_scaling_min_max_from_cpuinfo, isst-config.c:1788-1834): it returns -1 if cpu is not in present_cpumask. It opens the selected cpuinfo file read-only; if open fails it returns open's result (-1); it reads up to 16 bytes into a local buffer and closes the file; a negative read result is returned. It then opens the selected scaling file write-only (an open failure returns -1), forces byte 15 of the buffer to NUL, and writes strlen(buffer) bytes (which is not necessarily the number of bytes read) to it; a write result of -1 is returned after closing the file. Every descriptor it opened is closed before returning. In all other cases it returns 0, including when the read returned 0 bytes or the write wrote fewer bytes than requested.
note: reviewer (round15) right: returns 0 even if read() returns 0 or write() is short (isst-config.c:1807-1833); the failure returns from open/read/write are -1 (the old prose said 'negative error code' for open and read, which is -1 here).

name: isst_get_process_ctdp
prose: Precondition: id identifies a CPU/package, pkg_dev points to an isst_pkg_ctdp, and tdp_level is 0xff (all levels) or a level index. Postcondition (isst_get_process_ctdp, isst-core.c:368-468): it returns 0 immediately, touching nothing, if pkg_dev->processed is already set. Otherwise it calls isst_get_ctdp_levels and returns its nonzero result if it fails; it returns -1 (after displaying an 'Invalid level' message) if tdp_level is not 0xff and is greater than pkg_dev->levels; and if the package is not enabled it displays an informational message. For each selected level it records the level number, control CPU, package and die ids, and calls isst_get_ctdp_control; a nonzero result only skips that level (the loop continues, no error). For a level whose control info was read it sets pkg_dev->processed and the level's processed flag, reads the PBF info when supported (a failure there is ignored and pbf_found stays unset), reads the FACT info when supported (a nonzero result is returned), and then: if the package is not enabled and the platform is SKX based, it takes the base frequency from cpufreq (if > 0), reads the TRL ratios from the MSR and the TRL bucket info (their results ignored) and moves on to the next level, without allocating a core cpumask; otherwise it reads the TDP info and power info, allocates the level's core_cpumask (alloc_cpu_set), then reads the core mask, the TRL bucket info and the TRLs, returning the nonzero result of the first of these calls that fails (earlier fields of that level stay filled). After the loop, if no level had readable control info it displays an error message (pkg_dev->processed then stays 0); it returns 0 whenever it gets past the loop.
note: reviewer (round15) right: on the skx !enabled path the core_cpumask is not allocated and the trl-bucket result is ignored (isst-core.c:427-439); old prose also said errors were 'negative' (the code returns whatever nonzero value the helper returns) and presented the core_cpumask allocation as unconditional.
